FEATURED PROJECT / BUILT FROM EVERYDAY LIFE

01FULL-STACK WEB APPLICATION

My Payment Pro

A real household problem, turned into a personal tool.

I designed My Payment Pro to keep household purchases and reimbursement requests in one place, instead of relying on memory and scattered messages.

Visit website View repository

Source repository is private; access available on request.

01

Start with my own problem

I buy household supplies each month, but often forget to request reimbursement. For small purchases, sending another message each time also felt inconvenient.

02

Define the workflow

My idea was to record what I bought, what it was for, and how much I spent, then review everything together in a monthly summary.

03

Build with AI, then test

I defined the overall system concept and how I wanted to use it. Claude helped write the code; I tested the application and worked through bugs over several weeks.

Where I spent time debugging

Receipt uploads · Button interactions · Page speed · Mobile usability

I learned that generating code is only the starting point. I spent weeks testing and working through receipt-upload failures, unresponsive buttons, slow pages, and layouts that did not work on mobile.

  • Receipt uploadsAdded upload-in-progress and failure checks before saving, with separate receipt preview handling.
  • Search and filtersChanged the expense list to use updated server data instead of retaining a stale local copy.
  • Mobile layoutAdded a card-based expense list on small screens, keeping the table for larger screens.
  • Next.js 15
  • TypeScript
  • Supabase
  • Tesseract.js

System concept, requirements & hands-on testing · Claude-assisted coding

Project notes +
Problem / purpose
I buy household supplies each month, but often forget to request reimbursement. For small purchases, sending another message each time also felt inconvenient.
Solution
My idea was to record what I bought, what it was for, and how much I spent, then review everything together in a monthly summary.
Features / exploration
  • Sign up and sign in with Supabase Auth; expense data is separated by user account.
  • Create, edit, delete, and view expenses with dates, amounts, categories, and receipt images.
  • Search, filter by category, date range, and amount, then sort and paginate results.
  • Organize parent and child categories with custom colors and icons.
  • Dashboard with total spending, transaction counts, daily averages, trends, category breakdowns, and changes against a comparison period.
  • Expense calendar with daily totals and a list of expenses for the selected day.
  • Monthly reports with totals, category summaries, and expense details; export to PDF or print.
  • Read-only report links with expiration dates, revocation, and optional receipt access.
  • Tesseract.js OCR helps fill merchant names, dates, and totals, with keyword-based category suggestions. The current configuration focuses on English text.
Technology stack
  • Next.js 15 / React / TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS / Radix UI / Framer Motion
  • PostgreSQL / Supabase Auth / Supabase Storage
  • React Hook Form / Zod
  • TanStack Query / Zustand
  • Recharts
  • Tesseract.js
  • html2canvas / jsPDF
Technical implementation
  • Next.js App Router separates member pages, expense management, and APIs, using Server and Client Components as appropriate.
  • Relational expense, user, and category data with parent/child categories; Row Level Security (RLS) restricts expenses and categories to their owners.
  • Zod validates forms, and receipt uploads check file type and size.
  • OCR image reading, receipt-text parsing, and category suggestions are separate modules.
  • Dashboard calculations are separated from the UI and handle zero comparison baselines and month boundaries.
  • Reusable buttons, forms, tables, confirmation dialogs, and loading states keep the interface consistent.
Learning & practice
I learned that generating code is only the starting point. I spent weeks testing and working through receipt-upload failures, unresponsive buttons, slow pages, and layouts that did not work on mobile.
